A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DreamDistribution, with matching core methods, equations and experiments despite retitling and reformatting. Their main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, automatic metrics, human preferences, synthetic-data classification results, 3D demonstrations and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds personalization benchmarks, baseline comparisons, sensitivity studies and quantitative 3D-diversity results.

M1.justification: Both versions use frozen diffusion and text-encoder models, learnable prompts defining a Gaussian feature distribution, reparameterized sampling and the same diffusion-plus-orthogonality objective. Text editing, variance scaling and distribution interpolation are retained. Algorithm 1's explicit moment formulas clarify existing computations rather than establish a changed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds DreamBooth-dataset same-instance personalization, deliberately composed French Bulldog/dog/quadruped reference sets, and examples separating shared shape or object identity from varying texture or background (Appendix C). These substantially extend the tested task requirements and reference distributions. The original 12-scenario collection, ImageNet-100 evaluations and 3D applications remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Textual Inversion, DreamBooth and Custom Diffusion to the synthetic-data comparison, where v1 Table 2 compared against real data and prompt-engineering baselines. v2 also evaluates four-subset adaptations of these personalization methods, noise-perturbed Textual Inversion, and a Textual Inversion comparator for 3D generation (Table 3, Figure 13 and Table 5).

E3.justification: v2's main synthetic-data comparison explicitly gives learned methods the same 100 reference images per class; v1's headline DreamDistribution row corresponds to the retained 500-image setting. The reported human study increases from 10 annotators and 120 judgments to 20 and 240. New protocols include CLIP-T evaluation with 25 prompts and four images per prompt per scenario, within-set feature similarity for 3D diversity, and four-reference-image tests.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained prompt-count, training-set-size and real/synthetic-mixture analyses, v2 adds sensitivity studies for orthogonality weight and prompt-token count. Appendix C tests concept granularity, four-image reference sets, and preservation of invariant attributes against noise-perturbed Textual Inversion. These substantially broaden evidence about sensitivity, robustness and the source of diversity.

E5.justification: v1 Table 1 reports standard deviations alongside the quality-metric means; v2 Figure 4a retains the means but omits those deviations. Three-run averaging for synthetic-classifier experiments remains unchanged. The new 3D analysis says samples are generated 'without using random seeds,' but does not clearly specify seed handling.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical and qualitative results for new comparisons and analyses. For example, CLIP-T is 0.29 for DreamDistribution versus 0.33 for Custom Diffusion, and Table 5 reports 3D CLIP-I similarity of 0.53 versus Textual Inversion's 0.63. Human preference changes from 62.0% to 63.3% under the larger study. The original five quality-metric means remain unchanged. The main ImageNet score changes from 64.3% to 56.7% under different reference-set sizes; the 64.3% result remains in v2 Table 6, so this is not a same-setting decline.

T1.justification: The Gaussian modeling assumption, reparameterization derivation, losses and interpolation equations remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 expands the existing mean and variance calculations into explicit formulas. Neither version supplies a new theorem or proof, and v2 does not revise the formal mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: prompt-distribution learning for diverse personalized generation, text-guided control, transfer to 3D generation and synthetic training-data applications. The revised title and contribution wording do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes diminishing advantages at coarser concept granularity to difficulty capturing coherent distributions and increased outlier sampling. It also qualifies text-editing alignment because of distributional randomness and discusses the smaller benefit and longer training associated with additional prompt tokens. The original limitations about scarce, diverse references and restrictive Gaussian assumptions are retained in Appendix F.

D1.justification: v2 discloses reference-image counts for individual scenarios in Figure 11, baseline generation templates in Section 4.2, and explicit empirical moment computations in Algorithm 1. These clarify documentation without establishing changes to the original experiments. Most optimization and generation settings remain unchanged, while v1's project-website link is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds Alaluf et al. on personalization, Chen et al. and Ma et al. in support of the feature-space rationale, and Corso et al. for diversity measurement. The principal positioning relative to Textual Inversion and ProDA remains unchanged; the related-work discussion is not substantially reconceived.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, edits contribution and evaluation passages, expands dataset explanations, and moves the limitations section into Appendix F. The appendix gains additional subsections, but most existing introduction, method and conclusion prose and the overall narrative remain closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 switches to a single-column conference layout, redraws the method schematic and combines previously separate evaluation, control and 3D displays into multipanel figures. Tables and comparison galleries are substantially expanded, and Table 6 tabulates the previously plotted training-size analysis. The appendix text-editing figure drops the cat-expression and car-color examples, while other existing galleries are retained and resized.

improvement.justification: The matched-budget personalization comparisons and adapted-baseline controls address important gaps in v1's evidence for synthetic-data utility and distribution-based diversity. New sensitivity and concept-granularity analyses also clarify where the method's advantages weaken (v2 Table 1 and Appendices C–D). These substantially strengthen empirical support and interpretation, outweighing the removal of standard-deviation reporting and the project link.
